<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-cumin" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-cumin-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of cumin, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, cumin, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (65.8 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (312 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in EMRO (52 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (80.6 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, lead across 13 groups of cumin ranged from 300 µg/kg (Branded category, sample 6) to 2,800 µg/kg (Branded category, sample 2); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/alam2022-dhaka-spices-lead|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alam M Nur E, Hosen M Mozammal, Maksud M A, Khan S R, Lutfa L N, Choudhury Tasrina Rabia, Quraishi Shamshad B · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alam2022-dhaka-spices-lead">Lead Exposure of Four Biologically Important Common Branded and Nonbranded Spices: Relative Analysis and Health Implication</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Research Square (preprint)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alam2022-dhaka-spices-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 4 groups of cumin ranged from 168 µg/kg (US baby-food manufacturer B, ingredient lot, test date 11/3/2017) to 645 µg/kg (US baby-food manufacturer B, ingredient lot, test date 5/21/2018); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. House of Representatives, Committee on Oversight and Reform, Subcommittee on Economic and Consumer Policy · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Baby Foods Are Tainted with Dangerous Levels of Arsenic, Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Staff Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in cumin is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">
